newsitem.title: EGYPT: Housing shares pull Egyptian market down.
newsitem.headline: Housing shares pull Egyptian market down.

text.p: Housing shares pulled the Egyptian stock market down on Monday as real estate giant Medinet Nasr Housing and Development lost half of Sunday's gains.
Sister company Heliopolis Housing and Development continued to fall, shedding 25.81 pounds to end at 489.58.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index slipped 0.21 points to close at 321.89.
Turnover was an average 39.33 million pounds ($11.6 million), dominated by Medinet Nasr shares worth 10.8 million and Heliopolis Housing shares worth over four million.
Medinet Nasr closed at 406.10, down from 412.00 pounds.
The two companies were among the fastest risers among the partially privatised newcomers to the stock exchange last year but their P/E ratios are now way above the market average.

The most active shares were mixed in the cement sector, another bastion of the Cairo market. Suez Cement fell 0.45 to 64.00 while Egyptian Tora Portland Cement rose sharply, to 84.25 pounds from 81.50 on Sunday.

Trade in Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries shares was unusually busy and they gained 3.01 pounds to close at 83.01. Because of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, brokers were not available to say why.
In the milling sector, the two Nile Delta flour companies rose, Central and West Delta by 3.85 to 90.99 in large volume. But North Cairo lost 3.00 to 140.00.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 513.36 from 509.39 points on Sunday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 218.48 from 219.79.
Out of 81 shares traded, 27 advanced, 32 declined and the other 22 ended the day unchanged.
